providers.name: Google Play (GMS)
providers.desc: For devices with Google Play services. Uses Google Maps and Google location services.

providers.name: Huawei AppGallery (HMS)
providers.desc: For Huawei devices without Google Play services. Uses Huawei Map Kit, Location Kit and ML Kit (document scanning) instead.

variants.name: SDK without tracking
variants.desc: Only the Almatar SDK. No analytics, attribution, engagement or session-replay tools are included, and the SDK's analytics calls do nothing.

variants.name: SDK with tracking tools
variants.desc: The Almatar SDK plus the optional com.almatar:analytics-tracking add-on. Tracking runs only inside the Almatar flows (hotel, flight and bookings screens). The add-on registers itself at app startup, so no code changes are needed.

flows.name: B2C
flows.desc: Consumer integration. Initialize with enableB2bSDK = false and launch any of the hotel / flight / bookings flows directly. brandName is required for any partner without a website.
flows.init:
AlmatarAppInitializer.init(
    application = this,
    baseUrl = "<your base url>",
    almatarEnvironment = AlmatarEnvironment.Production,
    supportNumber = "<support number>",
    almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(),
    enableB2bSDK = false,
    // Required for any partner without a website
    brandName = "<your brand>",
)

flows.name: B2B
flows.desc: Corporate (e.g. Aamal) integration. Initialize with enableB2bSDK = true and a brandName (required for any partner without a website). Same launch flows as B2C, with the corporate section enabled on payment.
flows.init:
AlmatarAppInitializer.init(
    application = this,
    baseUrl = "<your base url>",
    almatarEnvironment = AlmatarEnvironment.Production,
    supportNumber = "<support number>",
    almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(),
    enableB2bSDK = true,
    brandName = "<your brand>",
)

flows.name: B2B with SSO
flows.desc: Corporate SSO integration. Initialize in B2B mode, then hand the SDK a short-lived SSO token via launchB2BSsoBookings. Only the SSO bookings entry point is valid in this flow.

payment.intro: Every launch function that opens a search or booking flow (`launchFlights`, `launchFlightsSearchResults`, `launchHotels`, `launchHotelsSearchResults`) takes `startPaymentFlowImpl`. It decides who takes the payment when the user taps pay. The SDK checks the price, and any coupon, first.

modes.name: Pay through Almatar
modes.summary: Pass `startPaymentFlowImpl = null`. Almatar shows its own payment screen, charges the user and confirms the booking. Your app has nothing else to do.
points: The payment screen lists the payment methods Almatar has enabled for your account, such as card, Tabby or Tamara.
Coupons, wallet and loyalty points are hidden in SDK mode.
After a successful payment the SDK shows its booking confirmation screen.
modes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchHotels(
    locale = LOCALE.ENGLISH,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = { /* the user left the SDK */ },
    generateTokenImpl = { callback -> callback(token, refreshToken, null) },
    startPaymentFlowImpl = null, // Almatar takes the payment
)

modes.name: Pay through your app
modes.summary: Pass a `startPaymentFlowImpl` function. The SDK hides its payment methods, and when the user taps pay it calls your function with the booking. You charge the user in your own checkout, then report the result back through `paymentFlowCallback`.
points: `bookingId`: Almatar's booking ID. Keep it with your payment record.
`amount`: the total to charge, in the booking's base currency.
`bookingKey`: the key that identifies the booking in Almatar.
`productType`: `flight` or `hotel`.
How the money you collect reaches Almatar (settlement and invoicing) is agreed with the Almatar team. It isn't set in the SDK.

states.name: LOADING
states.desc: The SDK shows a loader over the payment screen.

states.name: SUCCESS
states.desc: Report it only once the charge is confirmed. The SDK shows its booking confirmation screen.

states.name: CANCELLED
states.desc: The user stays on the payment screen and can pay again.

states.name: FAILURE(message)
states.desc: The SDK shows your message on the payment screen. The user can pay again.

postBooking.summary: Add-ons bought after booking from My Trips (for example seats or baggage) are always paid through your app. Pass `startPostPaymentFlow` to `launchBookings`. Without it, the add-on checkout closes. On `SUCCESS` the SDK shows the add-on confirmation; on `FAILURE` it shows your message and closes the checkout.

payment.otherFlowsNote: Payment in this flow always goes through Almatar: `launchB2BSsoBookings` has no payment parameter.

customization.intro: SDK screens follow the `almatarUiConfig` you pass to `AlmatarAppInitializer.init`. Every field is optional: leave one out to keep Almatar's look.

sections.title: Brand colors
sections.summary: Pass your brand colors in code with `colors = AlmatarColors(...)`, instead of overriding Almatar's color resources in XML. Each color fills every Almatar color that plays that role, so you set a few colors, not each resource.

fields.name: primary
fields.desc: Buttons, links, selected tabs and icons.

fields.name: onPrimary
fields.desc: Text on primary buttons.

fields.name: primaryContainer
fields.desc: A light tint of `primary` behind chips, inputs and selected cards.

fields.name: highlightText
fields.desc: Highlighted text, for example on `primaryContainer`.

fields.name: overrides
fields.desc: Any other Almatar color: a map from `com.almatar.core.R.color.*` to a color. Applied last.

codes.label: Fixed colors
Material 3 theme

points: Each SDK screen reads the colors when it opens. Call `setColors` again when your theme changes, for example for dark mode. `setColors(null)` goes back to Almatar's colors.
Covers Compose screens, colors set in code, and colors in XML layouts and styles, including state selectors in `res/color`.
Icons and shapes drawn from XML drawables keep Almatar's colors for now.
Overriding `almatar_*` colors in your own `colors.xml` still works. Where both apply, colors passed in code win.

sections.title: Logo
sections.summary: Set `logoRes` to a drawable from your app, PNG or vector, to show your logo where the SDK shows Almatar's.

codes.label: Kotlin

points: Shown in the gift box on the payment screen (40dp) and in the header of the corporate registration screen.

From 1.0.0-alpha05, also shown on the ticket in the flight booking success animation, fitted inside a square without stretching. Behind a white or very light logo the ticket turns dark: your `AlmatarColors.primary` when it is dark enough, otherwise dark grey.
Use an image that still reads at small sizes. A square mark works best.
For dark mode, put a light version of the logo with the same name in `res/drawable-night/`. Android picks it automatically when the SDK screens are dark, so nothing changes in `init`.

sections.title: Your name in SDK text
sections.summary: Some SDK text names Almatar, such as "Almatar Booking ID" or "rooms left on almatar.com". Set `displayName` and the SDK shows your name there instead, in each language you run it in.

fields.name: default
fields.desc: Your name for any language not in `byLanguage`.

fields.name: byLanguage
fields.desc: A language code (`"ar"`, `"fr"`, ...) to your name in that language. The SDK screen's language picks the entry.

codes.label: Kotlin

points: Only text where Almatar is the brand changes. In Arabic, المطار also means "airport", so airport text stays as it is.

Running the SDK in a language other than English or Arabic (`LOCALE.OTHER`)? The SDK text falls back to English unless your app overrides the `almatar_*` strings for that language. Your name comes from `byLanguage` either way.
This is not the `brandName` you pass to `init`: that one identifies your account to Almatar and is never shown.

sections.title: Background, bars and back button
sections.summary: Match the screen background, status bar, toolbar and back button to your app.

fields.name: backgroundConfig
fields.desc: Screen background: `AlmatarBackgroundConfig.ColorResource(R.color.x)` or `DrawableResource(R.drawable.x)`.

fields.name: statusBarConfig
fields.desc: Status bar color, `AlmatarColorConfig.Resource(R.color.x)` or `Transparent`, and `lightIcons`.

fields.name: toolbarConfig
fields.desc: Toolbar color, as an `AlmatarColorConfig`.

fields.name: backButtonRes
fields.desc: Drawable for the toolbar's back button.

codes.label: Kotlin
codes.code:
almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(
    backgroundConfig = AlmatarBackgroundConfig.DrawableResource(R.drawable.app_background),
    statusBarConfig = AlmatarStatusBarConfig(colorConfig = AlmatarColorConfig.Transparent),
    toolbarConfig = AlmatarToolbarConfig(configColor = AlmatarColorConfig.Transparent),
    backButtonRes = R.drawable.ic_back,
)

sections.title: Dark mode
sections.summary: SDK screens and `AlmatarStaticPackages` are light by default, even when the device is in dark mode. Turn dark mode on with `enableDarkMode = true`; the SDK then follows the device's dark mode setting.

fields.name: enableDarkMode
fields.desc: Optional, default `false`. `false`: always light. `true`: light or dark, following the device.

codes.label: Kotlin

points: `AlmatarStaticPackages` sits inside your own screen. With dark mode off, its cards stay light even when your screen or the device is dark.
Turn it on only if your app supports dark mode too, so SDK screens match yours.
If you pass brand colors with `colors`, call `setColors` again when your theme changes (see Brand colors).

debugging.intro: Tools for checking the SDK while you integrate it. Use them in debug builds only.

sections.title: See network calls with Chucker
sections.summary: The SDK records its network calls with Chucker when you initialize it with `almatarEnvironment = AlmatarEnvironment.Development`. The published SDK ships Chucker's no-op library, which records nothing, so swap in the real library for your debug builds. Release builds keep the no-op one.

codes.label: Kotlin DSL
Groovy

points: Run a debug build and open an SDK screen. A "Recording HTTP activity" notification appears: tap it to see each request and response. On Android 13 and later, allow notifications for your app first.
Nothing shows with `AlmatarEnvironment.Production`, even in a debug build.
Keep Chucker's version the same as the SDK's, 4.3.1. If your app already adds Chucker, this swap also avoids duplicate class errors between the real and no-op libraries.
The check matches every configuration whose name contains `debug`, including flavored ones such as `gmsDebugRuntimeClasspath`.
Never ship Chucker in a release build: it stores requests and responses on the device, including tokens and personal data.

features.intro: Every flow the SDK opens, grouped by what you want to do. Call `AlmatarAppInitializer.init` once first (see Initialize). Each `launch*` function opens SDK screens on top of yours; when the user is done, the SDK calls your `almatarFlowFinishedCallback`.

sections.title: Find the function you need
sections.summary: Pick what you want the user to do, then open its section from the sidebar.

fields.name: launchFlights
fields.desc: Flights: open the flight search.

fields.name: launchFlightsSearchResults
fields.desc: Flights: skip the search and open results for a trip you pass in.

fields.name: launchFlightConfirmation
fields.desc: Flights: open the confirmation of an existing booking.

fields.name: launchHotels
fields.desc: Hotels: open the hotel search.

fields.name: launchHotelsSearchResults
fields.desc: Hotels: skip the search and open results for a stay you pass in.

fields.name: launchHotelConfirmation
fields.desc: Hotels: open the confirmation of an existing booking.

fields.name: getStaticPackagesLandingPages
fields.desc: Static packages: get the landing pages as data, with no UI.

fields.name: AlmatarStaticPackages
fields.desc: Static packages: a composable that shows the package cards inside your screen.

fields.name: launchBookings
fields.desc: My bookings: the user's trips, with add-ons after booking.

fields.name: preFillFlightPassengers
fields.desc: Fill the flight passenger forms with your users' details.

fields.name: preFillHotelPassenger
fields.desc: Fill the hotel guest form with your user's details.

fields.name: clearCachedFlightPassengers
fields.desc: Remove the flight passengers saved by `preFillFlightPassengers`.

fields.name: clearCachedHotelPassengers
fields.desc: Remove the hotel guest saved by `preFillHotelPassenger`.

fields.name: setupGlobalConfig
fields.desc: Limit hotel and airport search to Saudi Arabia, or allow all countries.

sections.title: Parameters every launch takes
sections.summary: All `launch*` functions share these parameters, so the sections below show only what is different.

fields.name: locale
fields.desc: Language of the SDK screens: `LOCALE.ENGLISH` or `LOCALE.ARABIC`.

fields.name: almatarFlowFinishedCallback
fields.desc: Called when the user leaves the SDK, for example "Back to home" on a confirmation. Show your own screen here.

fields.name: generateTokenImpl
fields.desc: The SDK asks for your user's token. Call the callback with `(token, refreshToken, errorMessage)`. In B2B mode the token is checked before any screen opens.

fields.name: startPaymentFlowImpl
fields.desc: `null`: Almatar takes the payment. Your function: your app takes it. See the Payment page.

fields.name: isHajj
fields.desc: Optional, default `false`. Set `true` when the booking is for Hajj.

fields.name: baseUrl
fields.desc: Optional. Overrides the base URL from `init` for this flow.

fields.name: sdkLaunchCallback
fields.desc: Optional. `onError(error)` is called when the launch fails (for example an invalid B2B token). No screen opens.

codes.label: Shared setup

sections.title: Flights
sections.summary: Open the flight search, jump straight to results for a trip you already know, or show the confirmation of a booking.

codes.label: Search
codes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchFlights(
    locale = locale,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = ::onFlowFinished,
    generateTokenImpl = ::generateToken,
    startPaymentFlowImpl = null,          // Almatar takes the payment
)

codes.label: Search results
codes.code:
// imports: com.almatar.model.sdk.*, com.almatar.model.flight.TripType,
//          com.almatar.search.passenger.CabinClass, java.time.LocalDate
val riyadh = FlightLocationData(
    id = "RUH", name = "King Khalid International Airport", cityName = "Riyadh",
    cityCode = "RUH", countryName = "Saudi Arabia", countryCode = "SA", type = "airport",
)
val jeddah = FlightLocationData(
    id = "JED", name = "King Abdulaziz International Airport", cityName = "Jeddah",
    cityCode = "JED", countryName = "Saudi Arabia", countryCode = "SA", type = "airport",
)
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchFlightsSearchResults(
    flightSearchData = FlightSearchData(
        tripType = TripType.ROUNDTRIP,    // ONEWAY, ROUNDTRIP or MULTICITY
        cabinClass = CabinClass.ECONOMY,  // ECONOMY, PREMIUM_ECONOMY, BUSINESS or FIRST
        adultCount = 1, childCount = 0, infantCount = 0,
        legs = listOf(                    // one leg per flight
            FlightSearchLeg(LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 1), riyadh, jeddah),
            FlightSearchLeg(LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 10), jeddah, riyadh),
        ),
        editEnabled = false,              // false: the user can't change the search
    ),
    locale = locale,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = ::onFlowFinished,
    generateTokenImpl = ::generateToken,
    startPaymentFlowImpl = null,
)

codes.label: Confirmation
codes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchFlightConfirmation(
    bookingKey = "Qk7RjeRRV9",            // the booking's key
    locale = locale,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = ::onFlowFinished,
    generateTokenImpl = ::generateToken,
)

points: `editEnabled` (default `false`) controls what the user can change. With `false`, the results screen opens the edit sheet on its own, with origin, destination, dates and passenger count locked; multi-city legs can't be added or removed. Only the cabin class can still change. The passenger forms are read-only. With `true`, everything can be changed.
To fill the passenger forms too, call `preFillFlightPassengers` first and launch from its `onComplete` (see Pre-fill passengers).
The confirmation takes no payment parameter: the booking is already paid.

sections.title: Hotels
sections.summary: Open the hotel search, jump straight to results in Makkah or Madinah, or show the confirmation of a booking.

codes.label: Search
codes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchHotels(
    locale = locale,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = ::onFlowFinished,
    generateTokenImpl = ::generateToken,
    startPaymentFlowImpl = null,
)

codes.label: Search results
codes.code:
// imports: com.almatar.model.sdk.*, java.time.LocalDate, java.time.ZoneOffset
fun millis(date: LocalDate) = date.atStartOfDay(ZoneOffset.UTC).toInstant().toEpochMilli()

AlmatarAppInitializer.launchHotelsSearchResults(
    hotelData = HotelSearchData(
        hotelsDestination = HotelsDestination.Makkah,   // Makkah or Madinah
        rooms = listOf(
            HotelSearchRooms(adultCount = 2, childrenBirthDates = listOf(LocalDate.of(2018, 5, 1))),
        ),
        checkInDate = millis(LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 1)),
        checkOutDate = millis(LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 4)),
        editEnabled = false,
    ),
    locale = locale,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = ::onFlowFinished,
    generateTokenImpl = ::generateToken,
    startPaymentFlowImpl = null,
)

codes.label: Confirmation
codes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchHotelConfirmation(
    publicKey = "zMLN1JgEkp",             // the booking's public key
    locale = locale,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = ::onFlowFinished,
    generateTokenImpl = ::generateToken,
)

points: One `HotelSearchRooms` per room. Children are given by birth date, so the SDK works out their ages.
`checkInDate` and `checkOutDate` are epoch milliseconds.

`editEnabled` (default `false`) controls what the user can change. With `false`, the results screen opens the edit sheet on its own, with destination and dates locked; rooms and guests can still change. The guest form (title, first name, last name and nationality) is read-only. With `true`, everything can be changed.
To fill the guest form, call `preFillHotelPassenger` first.

sections.title: Static packages
sections.summary: Show Almatar's static packages inside your own screen. Unlike the other flows, nothing opens until the user taps Book: you place the package cards where you want them. Booking opens the SDK's package details, payment and confirmation screens.

fields.name: getStaticPackagesLandingPages
fields.desc: Data only: the landing pages (`id`, `title`, `description`, images). Use it for your own UI or to choose a page id.

fields.name: AlmatarStaticPackages
fields.desc: Composable with the package cards of one landing page: `landingPageId`, or the first page when it is `null`.

codes.label: Show the cards (Compose)
Data only

points: `scrollable = false` (the default) gives the cards their full height, so they can be one section of your scrolling screen. Use `true` when the cards fill a screen on their own.

The cards have no padding of their own, so they line up with your content. Set the padding with `modifier`, for example `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(horizontal = 16.dp)`. Before 1.0.6-alpha05 the SDK added its own padding.
Changing `landingPageId` loads that page's packages.
On the confirmation, "Back to home" closes the package screens and calls `almatarFlowFinishedCallback`; "Go to My Trips" opens the bookings screen.
`getStaticPackagesLandingPages` delivers its result on the main thread. Calling it again before the result arrives cancels the earlier call.
Using views, not Compose? Put `AlmatarStaticPackages` in a `ComposeView`.

sections.title: My bookings
sections.summary: Open the user's trips. From there the user can see bookings and buy add-ons such as seats or baggage.

codes.label: My bookings

points: `startPostPaymentFlow` is optional. Without it, the add-on checkout closes. See the Payment page.
B2B with SSO uses `launchB2BSsoBookings` instead (see Initialize, B2B with SSO).

sections.title: Pre-fill passengers
sections.summary: Save your users' details before launching, so the SDK's passenger and guest forms are already filled in. Each call replaces what was saved before.

codes.label: Flight passengers
codes.code:
val passengers = listOf(
    FlightPassengerData(
        id = "2959",                      // your id, or null
        firstName = "John", lastName = "Doe",
        gender = Gender.Male,
        phoneNumber = 966 to "501234567", // (country code, number), or null
        email = "john@example.com",       // or null
        birthDate = LocalDate.of(1990, 1, 1),
        nationality = "sa",               // 2-letter ISO code
        documentType = PassengerDocumentType.NationalID,
        documentNumber = "1234567890",
        documentExpirationDate = LocalDate.of(2031, 6, 8),
    ),
)
AlmatarAppInitializer.preFillFlightPassengers(
    passengers = passengers,
    lastDepartureDate = LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 10),   // the last leg's date
) { adultCount, childCount, infantCount, errorMessage ->
    if (errorMessage != null) return@preFillFlightPassengers   // nothing was saved
    // Launch with the same counts, e.g. launchFlightsSearchResults(
    //     FlightSearchData(..., adultCount = adultCount!!, childCount = childCount!!, infantCount = infantCount!!, ...))
}

codes.label: Hotel guest

points: `nationality` must be a 2-letter ISO country code, such as `sa`, `eg` or `ae`.
Allowed `documentType`: Saudi and other GCC nationals `Passport` or `NationalID`; everyone else `Passport` or `Iqama`.
Ages are worked out on `lastDepartureDate`: under 2 is an infant, under 12 a child, otherwise an adult. `onComplete` returns these counts; launch with the same counts.
When `errorMessage` is not null, it lists every invalid passenger and nothing is saved.
The hotel guest is the main guest of the booking.

sections.title: Clear saved passengers
sections.summary: Remove the details saved by the pre-fill functions, for example when the user logs out or before a flow that should start with empty forms.

codes.label: Clear
codes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.clearCachedFlightPassengers()   // saved by preFillFlightPassengers
AlmatarAppInitializer.clearCachedHotelPassengers()    // saved by preFillHotelPassenger

points: Calling a pre-fill function again already replaces what was saved, so you don't need to clear before it.

sections.title: Search region
sections.summary: Choose which places the hotel and airport search suggests. Call it before launching, or pass `supportedCountry` to `init`.

fields.name: SupportedCountry.ALL
fields.desc: Default. Hotels and airports in every country.

fields.name: SupportedCountry.KSA
fields.desc: Only hotels and departure airports in Saudi Arabia.

codes.label: Search region
codes.code: AlmatarAppInitializer.setupGlobalConfig(supportedCountry = SupportedCountry.KSA)

migration.intro: Moving from `com.almatar.android:general-sdk` (7.3.x) to `com.almatar:core-gms` / `core-hms`. The SDK's packages and launch functions are the same, so most apps only change their Gradle files and the `init` call. Follow the steps in order; each shows your code before and after.

sections.title: What changes
sections.summary: Everything you need to touch. Anything not listed works as before: `AlmatarAppInitializer.launch*`, the pre-fill and cache functions, `com.almatar.model.sdk.*`, `AlmatarUiConfig`, and Hilt (your `Application` still needs `@HiltAndroidApp`).

fields.name: Artifact
fields.desc: `com.almatar.android:general-sdk` becomes `com.almatar:core-gms` (Google Play) or `com.almatar:core-hms` (Huawei).

fields.name: Repositories
fields.desc: The vendor repositories you added by hand are replaced by the `com.almatar.settings` Gradle plugin.

fields.name: Tracking tools
fields.desc: general-sdk always bundled UXCam, Insider, WebEngage, Adjust, Mixpanel and Firebase. Core has none; add `com.almatar:analytics-tracking` only if you want them.

fields.name: init
fields.desc: `enableB2B` is renamed `enableB2bSDK`, and `supportNumber` is a new required parameter.

fields.name: Resources
fields.desc: The SDK's `R` class moves from `com.almatar.R` to `com.almatar.core.R`. Resource names don't change.

fields.name: Build tools
fields.desc: Core needs newer Gradle, AGP, Kotlin and compileSdk. See Setup for the exact versions.

fields.name: Removed
fields.desc: `PaymentFeatureConfig.sdkShowCorporateSection`: B2B mode shows the corporate section on its own.

sections.title: 1. Update your build tools
sections.summary: Core is built with newer tools than general-sdk 7.3.70, so your app needs at least these versions.

fields.name: compileSdk
fields.desc: 36 → 37 (minSdk stays 26, JDK stays 17)

points: The Setup page always lists the requirements of the version you pick in the sidebar.

sections.title: 2. Replace the repositories with the settings plugin
sections.summary: Apply `com.almatar.settings` in `settings.gradle.kts` and remove the vendor repositories you added for general-sdk.

codes.label: Before (general-sdk)
After (core)

points: Using Groovy (`settings.gradle`)? The Setup page has the same block for Groovy.
Keep your `gpr.user` / `gpr.key` credentials: core is on the same GitHub Packages repository.

sections.title: 3. Change the dependency
sections.summary: Swap the general-sdk coordinate for core. Publishing to Huawei AppGallery too? Use a product flavor per store, as shown on Setup.

codes.label: Before (general-sdk)
After (core)

points: Never put `core-gms` and `core-hms` in the same build variant: they contain the same classes.
Use an exact version, not a range or `latest`: older 1.0.x builds still bundle the tracking tools.

sections.title: 4. Update init
sections.summary: Rename `enableB2B` to `enableB2bSDK` and pass your `supportNumber`. Everything else in the call is unchanged.

codes.label: Before (general-sdk)
After (core)
codes.code:
// core
AlmatarAppInitializer.init(
    application = this,
    baseUrl = "<your base url>",
    almatarEnvironment = AlmatarEnvironment.Production,
    supportNumber = "<support number>", // new, required
    almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(),
    enableB2bSDK = false,  // true for the B2B flow
    // Required for any partner without a website
    brandName = "<your brand>",
)

points: `enableSDK` is new and defaults to `true`; leave it out.
Set `enableB2bSDK = true` only for the B2B flow (corporate partners, including B2B with SSO). B2C apps keep it `false`, the default.
`brandName` is required for any partner without a website, in B2C and B2B. Partners with a website can leave it out.

sections.title: 5. Fix code that referenced the SDK
sections.summary: Most apps compile without changes after step 4. Check for these:

codes.label: Resources

points: Overriding SDK resources in your own `res/` (same name, `almatar_` prefix) keeps working.
Remove any use of `PaymentFeatureConfig.sdkShowCorporateSection`.

If you relied on the tracking tools general-sdk bundled (events in your dashboards, push via the SDK), add `com.almatar:analytics-tracking` and apply `com.almatar.settings.tracking` instead of `com.almatar.settings`.

sections.title: 6. Check the migration
points: Run `./gradlew :app:dependencies` and confirm `com.almatar:core-gms` (or `core-hms`) is there and `com.almatar.android:general-sdk` is gone.
Open each flow you use (hotels, flights, bookings) and complete a booking in your test environment.
B2B: launch once with a valid and once with an invalid token, and check that `sdkLaunchCallback.onError` is called for the invalid one.
New in core: brand colors, your display name and static packages. See Customize the UI and Features.

versions.notes: AlmatarStaticPackages no longer adds its own padding around the cards: set it with the modifier you pass, for example Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(horizontal = 16.dp). Without it the cards now reach the edges of their space. See Features.

permissions.name: com.google.android.providers.gsf.permission.READ_GSERVICES
permissions.from: Fingerprint Pro, used by Checkout.com fraud checks

tools.name: UXCam
tools.purpose: Session replay and heatmaps; passenger and payment fields are masked

tools.name: Firebase Messaging
